claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To start, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's my only child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex! I have a few questions to help determine your eligibility.

First, could you tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 17, his eligibility will depend on his current situation.

Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar), or enrolled on an approved training course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in college or doing A-levels or anything like that. But he has just started an apprenticeship actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

Since Alex is on an apprenticeship, I need to ask a couple more questions about it:

Is Alex's apprenticeship a paid apprenticeship (i.e., does he receive wages or a salary for it)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's a paid apprenticeship - he gets wages for it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Unfortunately, a paid apprenticeship is considered employment rather than approved education or training for Child Benefit purposes. Child Benefit can only continue for 16-19 year olds if they are in:

- Full-time non-advanced education (e.g., A-levels, GCSEs, NVQs up to level 3), or
- An approved unpaid training course

Since Alex is 17 and on a **paid** apprenticeship, he would not meet the criteria for you to continue receiving Child Benefit for him.

Before I confirm this, could I just check: are you currently living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. So just to be clear, even though he's only 17 and still doing training, I can't get Child Benefit for him because the apprenticeship is paid?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, that's correct. Even though Alex is only 17 and is receiving training through his apprenticeship, the key factor is that it's a **paid** apprenticeship. Because he's earning wages, it's treated as employment rather than qualifying education or training for Child Benefit purposes.

Child Benefit is designed to support children who are either:
- Under 16, or
- 16-19 and in **full-time non-advanced education** or on an **approved unpaid training course**

Since Alex's apprenticeship is paid, he doesn't fall into either of these categories, so unfortunately you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.

Let me now confirm this outcome for you.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment:

**You are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

**Reason:** Alex is 17 years old and on a paid apprenticeship. For young people aged 16-19, Child Benefit can only be claimed if they are in full-time non-advanced education or on an approved unpaid training course. Since Alex's apprenticeship is paid, it counts as employment, which means he doesn't meet the qualifying criteria.

I'm sorry this isn't the outcome you were hoping for. If Alex's circumstances change in the future—for example, if he were to leave the apprenticeship and return to full-time education before turning 20—you may be able to make a new claim at that point.

Is there anything else you'd like me to help clarify?
